voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: One recorded call said it was from a data service provider for Google. This is your final notice. If you do not act soon, Google will label your business as permanently closed.
It wasn't Google. It was Pointbreak Media, a Florida telemarketer. Claiming a Google listing is free.
In seven weeks of twenty seventeen, Pointbreak made nearly seventy-five million robocalls. Nearly fifteen million to numbers on the Do Not Call Registry.
Owners who pressed one paid three to five hundred dollars to claim and verify it. The court found no evidence customers benefited. Co-owner Dustin Pillonato admitted clients saw zero benefits.

On October twentieth, twenty seventeen, their card processor cut them off. The next week, Pointbreak wrote itself one-hundred-dollar checks from at least two hundred eighty customers' accounts, without consent. Justin Ramsey endorsed every one.

Both men were already under court injunctions. In twenty nineteen, a federal judge ordered them to pay more than three point three million dollars, and hand over fifty-three pieces of jewelry. The product was a final notice, about something that was always free.
